title: Private deployment: resilient metering aggregator for deferred sync and offline reconciliation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers running Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) need accurate, auditable usage reporting for billing and quota enforcement even when their control plane cannot reach Redwood continuously. Current lightweight exporters rely on near-real-time sync and can drop records during prolonged air-gapped periods or network partitions. This causes incorrect invoices, quota misalignment, and operator overhead to reconcile accounts after the fact.

Goal: Build a resilient local metering aggregator and reconciliation flow that: 1) reliably persists usage at the edge with tamper-evident sequencing, 2) supports delayed bulk export and incremental delta sync, 3) provides deterministic reconciliation and conflict-resolution rules, and 4) integrates with rate-limit enforcement to avoid silent quota breaches during offline windows.
acceptance_criteria: Edge aggregator persists all request-level usage events for up to 90 days with configurable retention
Exports can run in incremental mode (seq windows) and full-batch mode; both result in idempotent consumption on the control plane
Reconciliation job on the control plane detects gaps/duplicates and produces an audit report mapping to invoiced token counts
Rate-limit enforcement on the appliance falls back to local quota accounting and throttles requests when local tokens exhausted
End-to-end integration test demonstrating a 72-hour offline window with 0% silent under-billing and reconciliation delta <= 0.1%
Operational docs + troubleshooting runbook and metrics for export success/failure, backlog size, and reconciliation drift
technical_design:
We will introduce an on-appliance Metering Aggregator (MA) service that receives per-request usage records from the local inference runtime. Records will be appended to an immutable write-ahead log (WAL) segmented by day and signed with the node's key to provide tamper evidence. The MA exposes two export modes: a streaming incremental exporter that sends sequence ranges and a bulk export that uploads compressed day segments via the secure transport when connectivity is available. Exports include checksums and sequence metadata.

On the control plane side, implement an idempotent ingestion API that accepts sequence ranges or full segments and performs deduplication by (node-id, segment-id, seq-num). A reconciliation worker will compute expected vs received deltas, applying business rules: prefer aggregator counts for overlaps, use control-plane-merged counters for partial uploads, and flag manual review when reconciliation drift exceeds threshold.

Quota enforcement: when the control plane is unreachable, the appliance consults a local quota ledger with periodic checkpointing. The ledger uses optimistic counters and reserves buckets for long-running requests to avoid double-counting on reconnect. When local quota is exhausted, the runtime responds with 429 and logs the event for audit.

Telemetry: expose metrics for backlog_bytes, last_export_seq, export_failures, wal_corruption_count, local_quota_headroom, and reconciliation_drift_pct. All metrics pushed to hosted telemetry when control plane is available and stored locally otherwise.
implementation_notes: MA service will be Rust-based microservice reusing existing local-collector proto for compact events
WAL format: newline-delimited compressed protobufs with Ed25519 signatures per segment
Encryption at rest via customer KMS key if provided; otherwise node-key with rotation support
Export protocol piggybacks existing appliance-controlplane TLS channel with mutual auth
Control-plane dedupe index stored in CockroachDB by (node_id, segment_id, seq) with TTL for old segments
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: WAL growth could overwhelm on-prem disk during extended offline periods. Mitigation: configurable retention/TTL + backpressure to runtime (drop non-critical telemetry), early alert on backlog threshold.

Risk: Inconsistent clocks across nodes leading to segment overlaps. Mitigation: use sequence numbers generated by MA and wall-clock only for retention policies; reconcile by sequence ranges.

Risk: Customers concerned about tamperability. Mitigation: sign segments and include optional customer-provided KMS/HSM binding; provide audit report and playback tool.
qa_plan: 1) Unit tests for WAL append/read, signature verification, and exporter checksum. 2) Integration tests: simulated network partition for 72h with burst traffic and subsequent multi-segment export. 3) Load test: sustained 1000 rps generation on a single appliance and measurement of disk and CPU. 4) End-to-end billing simulation mapping ingested events to invoiced token counts with seeded duplicates and gaps.
rollout_plan:
Stage 1: feature behind 'local_metering_v2' feature flag; deploy to Canary customers (internal + two partner POCs). Stage 2: collect metrics and iterate on backpressure heuristics. Stage 3: open to general availability for Private customers with documentation and billing notice window.

Fallback: if reconciliation drift > 1% during canary, automatically disable bulk automatic billing and require manual verification for affected invoices.
comments: 2025-02-19 Aisha Patel: Initial scoping completed. Spikes planned to validate WAL throughput and signature overhead. Added risk section.
2025-02-25 Diego Martinez: PoC WAL implementation shows ~12% CPU overhead and 45MB/min disk at 500 rps; will optimize protobuf packing and enable on-the-fly compression.

2025-03-01 Riley Chen: Reviewed ingestion idempotency design; suggested adding segment-level checksums and stronger dedupe keys. Also requested explicit acceptance criterion for rate-limit behavior during offline windows.
2025-03-04 Samir Rao: Ops approved telemetry set and runbook. Requested additional alerting for backlog_bytes > 20GB.
